agree.reason: The GM gets a credible insider case: seven weeks covering the job, turnover and training numbers, and an open admission that the renovation drove much of the score gain. But it never sets the writer's experience against the outside candidate's larger-hotel background, so the main reason to pick someone else is left unanswered.

honest.reason: It rightly declines to claim the writer was the main reason scores rose. A few lines go beyond the brief, though: 'without lowering the standard' and 'without a gap in leadership' are not supported by any fact given.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out turnover falling from 64% to 36% and training getting 44% faster. It doesn't turn those into anything concrete, such as about 4 fewer shadow shifts per new hire or roughly 4 fewer departures a year, and it calls a 44% drop 'nearly half' without showing the figure.

right_comparison.reason: The before-and-after turnover comparison is fair. The comparison that actually matters is the writer against an outside hire, who would have no knowledge of this team or property and would arrive after a seven-week vacancy, and the document never makes it.

qualification.reason: The budget plan names a weekly payroll review and a 60/90-day window, but these are left as placeholders. It sets no measurable bar for being ready, such as payroll within a set percentage of budget, and says nothing about what happens if that bar is missed.

objections.reason: The renovation objection and the missing budget experience are both met head-on. The outside candidate's experience at a larger hotel is never addressed.

fit.reason: It is a memo of about one page, as asked, but it still has several unfilled bracket placeholders, including the closing goals section, so it can't be sent as it stands.
